stem: What is the Common Service Data Model (CSDM)?

options.text: A standard, prescriptive framework for how to organize service and CI data in the CMDB across ServiceNow products
A separate database that replaces the CMDB
A discovery tool that scans the network

rationale: CSDM is a blueprint, not a product: it prescribes where service-related data and CIs should live in the standard CMDB tables so that ITSM, ITOM, SecOps, and APM all interpret the data the same way. It's about consistent structure, not a new database or scanner.

distractor_notes.B: CSDM organizes the existing CMDB; it doesn't replace it with a separate database.
distractor_notes.C: Discovery scans the network; CSDM is a data-model framework.
distractor_notes.D: CSDM is a data standard, not a licensing model.

stem: Which set best represents the service domains of the CSDM framework?

options.text: Foundation, Design, Build, Manage Technical Services, and Sell/Consume

rationale: CSDM organizes data into service domains — Foundation (core data), Design, Build, Manage Technical Services, and Sell/Consume — each holding the appropriate service and CI constructs. The other options are ITSM processes, status colors, and Discovery phases, not CSDM domains.

distractor_notes.B: Those are ITSM processes, not CSDM domains.
distractor_notes.C: Status colors aren't CSDM domains.
distractor_notes.D: Those are Discovery phases, not CSDM domains.

stem: CSDM describes an adoption journey using which sequence of maturity stages?
rationale: CSDM frames adoption as Crawl → Walk → Run → Fly, building on a Foundation, so organizations mature incrementally rather than attempting everything at once. Each stage unlocks more capability as data completeness and modeling improve.

distractor_notes.B: Bronze/Silver/Gold isn't the CSDM maturity model.
distractor_notes.C: Alpha/Beta/GA are software release phases, not CSDM stages.
distractor_notes.D: Plan-Do-Check-Act is a generic improvement cycle, not CSDM's stages.

stem: A CSDM Data Manager wants metrics on alignment of product models, locations, and business units. These data elements belong to which CSDM domain/stage?
rationale: Foundation holds the core, broadly shared data — companies, locations, users, groups, product models, and business units — that everything else builds on. Aligning these is the first step (the basis of the Crawl stage) before modeling services.

distractor_notes.B: Sell/Consume covers service offerings and business services consumed, not core reference data.
distractor_notes.C: Manage Technical Services covers application/technical services, not product models and locations.
distractor_notes.D: Design holds business applications and related design data, not the core foundation entities.

stem: In CSDM, what does a Business Application represent?

options.text: A software application viewed from a business/architecture perspective, independent of where it is deployed
A single running process on one server

rationale: A Business Application is the logical, business-level concept of an application (e.g., 'Payroll') — what the organization recognizes and funds — separate from its concrete deployed instances. Those deployed instances are modeled as Application Services related to the Business Application.

distractor_notes.B: A single running process maps to a deployed Application Service instance, not the Business Application concept.
distractor_notes.C: A switch is infrastructure, not a business application.
distractor_notes.D: An incident is an ITSM record, not a CSDM application construct.

stem: What does an Application Service represent in CSDM?

options.text: A deployed, running instance of an application and its supporting CIs that together deliver a service
The legal owner of the data center

rationale: An Application Service models an actual deployment — the application instance plus the servers, databases, and other CIs that support it — typically built by Service Mapping or tags. It's the concrete, mapped service that impact analysis and monitoring use.

distractor_notes.B: Ownership of a facility isn't what an Application Service models.
distractor_notes.C: A mailbox is an endpoint artifact, not an application service.
distractor_notes.D: A change template is an ITSM construct, not a CSDM service.

stem: A customer wants to model their business applications and capture the different types of data they handle, including Personally Identifiable Information (PII). Which CSDM construct represents this data?
rationale: The Information Object captures the data/information an application handles — including sensitive categories like PII — and relates it to the Business Application. That linkage supports privacy, security, and compliance use cases that need to know where regulated data lives.

distractor_notes.B: Business Capability expresses what the business does, not the data handled.
distractor_notes.C: Product Model describes a model of hardware/software, not data categories.
distractor_notes.D: Service Offering defines a service's commitments, not the data it processes.

stem: How does a Service Offering differ from the Service it is based on in CSDM?

options.text: A Service Offering is a specific variation of a service with defined commitments (e.g., levels, SLAs, audience), while the Service is the general definition
A Service Offering is a type of incident
A Service is always retired before an Offering exists

rationale: A Service is the general thing provided; a Service Offering packages it with specific commitments — service levels, supported hours, audience, or cost. One service can have multiple offerings (e.g., Gold vs Silver), which is how CSDM expresses tiered or varied delivery.

distractor_notes.B: They're related but distinct: general service vs committed offering.
distractor_notes.C: A Service Offering isn't an incident type.
distractor_notes.D: Offerings exist for active services; no such retirement rule applies.

stem: A CMDB Administrator notices CIs do not have a Support group. Which CSDM construct can automatically populate and maintain the support group on CI records?

options.text: A Technical (Technology Management) Service Offering related to the CIs

rationale: Technical Service Offerings carry support and ownership group information, and when CIs are aligned to an offering (often via dynamic groups), those group values flow onto the CIs and stay maintained. It's the model-driven way to keep support assignment consistent rather than editing each CI.

distractor_notes.B: A health dashboard measures quality; it doesn't populate support groups.
distractor_notes.C: Knowledge articles don't set CI support groups.
distractor_notes.D: An SLA governs response times, not CI group population.

stem: A customer's CMDB is aligned to the CSDM 'Walk' stage. Which benefit does this enable?

options.text: Impact assessments for incident, problem, and change against Business Services / Application Services

rationale: By the Walk stage, services are mapped and related to their supporting CIs, which unlocks service-aware impact analysis — seeing how an incident, problem, or change affects business and application services. That service context is the core payoff of progressing past Foundation/Crawl.

distractor_notes.B: Walk is well beyond raw storage; services are modeled and usable.
distractor_notes.C: CSDM maturity doesn't eliminate incidents.
distractor_notes.D: Discovery still feeds the CMDB regardless of CSDM stage.

stem: Why is following CSDM important when populating the CMDB?

options.text: It places data in consistent, expected locations so ITSM, ITOM, SecOps, and APM can all use it reliably
It makes the CMDB load faster
It removes the need for governance
It is only relevant to the finance team

rationale: CSDM's value is interoperability: when everyone models services and CIs the same way, the many products and processes that read the CMDB get predictable, trustworthy data. Off-model data may technically exist but breaks the downstream features that expect CSDM placement.

distractor_notes.B: CSDM is about correct structure and usability, not load speed.
distractor_notes.C: CSDM complements governance; it doesn't replace it.
distractor_notes.D: CSDM underpins enterprise-wide processes, not just finance.

stem: Which TWO are business values of a well-maintained CMDB aligned to CSDM?

options.text: Streamlining incident and change management with service context

rationale: A trusted, CSDM-aligned CMDB makes the organization more resilient (you understand dependencies and impact) and makes core processes like incident and change faster and safer with real service context. Payroll and email are unrelated systems.

distractor_notes.C: Payroll generation isn't a CMDB function.
distractor_notes.D: The CMDB doesn't replace email systems.

stem: Which two ways does the Change Management process benefit from a CSDM-aligned CMDB?

options.text: Understanding the impact of a change on related services
Identifying blackout/maintenance windows relevant to the affected CIs/services
Automatically writing the change's code fix
Determining the root cause of an unrelated incident

rationale: With services mapped to their CIs, change planners can see what a change will affect and respect the blackout/maintenance windows tied to those CIs and services. CSDM doesn't write code, and root-cause analysis is Problem Management's job.

distractor_notes.C: Code remediation is development work, not a CSDM/change benefit.
distractor_notes.D: Root-cause analysis belongs to Problem Management, not change impact.

stem: Which two advantages does ServiceNow Event Management gain from a well-populated, CSDM-aligned CMDB?

options.text: Binding alerts to the specific CIs they originate from
Mapped services provide visibility into the business impact of an alert
Automatically resolving every alert without analysis
Eliminating the need for monitoring tools

rationale: A good CMDB lets Event Management tie alerts to the exact CIs involved and, through mapped services, show which business/application services an alert threatens. That turns raw alerts into prioritized, impact-aware action — but it doesn't auto-resolve alerts or replace monitoring tools.

distractor_notes.C: Event Management still requires analysis/correlation; it doesn't blindly auto-resolve.
distractor_notes.D: Monitoring tools generate the events; the CMDB adds context, not replacement.

stem: Which two benefits does a CSDM-aligned CMDB provide to Security Operations (Vulnerability and Security Incident Response)?

options.text: Identifying which IT infrastructure has a given vulnerability
Helping the security team assess and remediate based on affected CIs and their service context
Automatically patching every vulnerability with no action

rationale: SecOps uses the CMDB to pinpoint which assets carry a vulnerability and to understand the services and ownership around them, so remediation can be prioritized by business impact. It doesn't auto-patch everything or replace the scanners that detect issues.

distractor_notes.C: The CMDB informs prioritization; it doesn't auto-resolve vulnerabilities.
distractor_notes.D: Scanning tools find vulnerabilities; the CMDB adds asset/service context.

stem: An organization is changing data centers and wants to understand the consequences. How can Application Service mapping support Change Management here?

options.text: By revealing the business impact of the CIs involved, showing which services are affected by the move
By listing the physical color of each server

rationale: Application Service maps connect infrastructure CIs to the services they support, so moving a data center can be assessed for which services and business functions will be disrupted. That impact visibility is exactly what change planning for a migration needs.

distractor_notes.B: Cosmetic details don't inform change impact.
distractor_notes.C: Mapping informs decisions; it doesn't auto-approve changes.
distractor_notes.D: Service mapping doesn't author migration scripts.

stem: A governance team is transitioning from legacy CMDB status fields to CSDM life cycle status fields. Which table holds the mapping between legacy values and CSDM life cycle stages?
rationale: The Life Cycle Mapping table is where legacy status values are mapped to the standardized CSDM life cycle stage/status, enabling a controlled transition. Editing the mappings is how the team aligns existing data to the CSDM lifecycle model without losing meaning.

distractor_notes.B: The incident table stores incidents, not lifecycle mappings.
distractor_notes.C: User records don't hold CI lifecycle mappings.
distractor_notes.D: Knowledge articles are unrelated to lifecycle status mapping.

stem: After selecting 'Enable Life Cycle field mappings' to align CIs with CSDM, what is the recommended next step?

options.text: Resolve any incomplete mappings flagged in the Discrepancy Report before activating
Immediately delete all legacy status values

rationale: Enabling lifecycle mappings produces a discrepancy report of legacy values that don't yet map cleanly. Resolving those gaps first ensures every CI lands on a valid CSDM lifecycle stage when you activate, avoiding orphaned or mis-stated statuses.

distractor_notes.B: Deleting legacy values before mapping loses the information needed to translate them.
distractor_notes.C: Disabling health is unrelated to enabling lifecycle mappings.
distractor_notes.D: Retiring CIs is not a step in enabling lifecycle mappings.

stem: Where does a CMDB Administrator obtain the CMDB / CSDM Data Foundations Dashboard?

options.text: It is available as a free application on the ServiceNow Store
It must be coded from scratch
It is only available by contacting sales for a quote

rationale: The Data Foundations Dashboard is distributed as a free application on the ServiceNow Store, so administrators install it to measure and remediate CSDM/CMDB data alignment. It isn't something you build by hand or purchase separately.

distractor_notes.B: It is installable from the Store.
distractor_notes.C: It's a packaged app, not a build-it-yourself artifact.
distractor_notes.D: It's free on the Store, not a paid sales engagement.

stem: A CMDB Administrator runs a Data Foundations playbook (e.g., 'Services Have Owners Identified') to remediate issues shown on the Data Foundations Dashboard. Which TWO types of remediation activities do these playbooks support?

options.text: Analyze data (understand the gap and its scope)

rationale: Data Foundations playbooks guide a structured remediation: analyze the issue (which records, how many, why) and then fix the data to close the gap. They're about understanding and correcting specific data problems, not destructive actions like wiping the CMDB or killing sources.

distractor_notes.C: Playbooks remediate targeted gaps; they don't delete the CMDB.
distractor_notes.D: Disabling data sources isn't a playbook remediation step.

stem: Why does ServiceNow recommend an incremental CSDM adoption (Crawl before Run) rather than modeling everything at once?

options.text: Because solid Foundation data must exist before advanced service modeling delivers reliable value; maturity builds in stages
Because CSDM cannot model services at all
Because each stage must take exactly one year
Because Run is easier than Crawl

rationale: Advanced service modeling and impact analysis are only as good as the Foundation beneath them, so CSDM staging gets the core data right first, then layers on services and offerings. Trying to model everything before the basics are clean produces unreliable maps and wasted effort.

distractor_notes.B: CSDM is centrally about modeling services; this is false.
distractor_notes.C: There's no fixed one-year-per-stage rule.
distractor_notes.D: Crawl (foundation) precedes Run for a reason; Run isn't simply 'easier'.

stem: Per CSDM, a server team requests a catalog item for infrastructure upgrade requests. Which role is most appropriate to own/initiate the technical service side of this?
rationale: Infrastructure/technical services and their offerings are owned by Technical Service Owners, who are accountable for those services in the CSDM model. Enterprise Architects work at the design/business-application layer, and the other roles are unrelated to technical service ownership.

distractor_notes.B: Enterprise Architects focus on design/business architecture, not technical service ownership of infrastructure offerings.
distractor_notes.C: A customer service agent handles cases, not technical service ownership.
distractor_notes.D: Payroll administration is unrelated to technical services.

stem: A Service Portfolio Manager wants to know which Application Services their Business Service Offerings depend on. Modeling this dependency relationship is characteristic of which CSDM maturity stage?

options.text: It is never modeled in CSDM

rationale: Relating business/service offerings to the application services they depend on is service-mapping work that comes together at the Walk stage, once Foundation data and service models are in place. Foundation/Crawl establish the basics but don't yet wire these service dependencies for portfolio insight.

distractor_notes.B: Foundation holds core data, not these service dependency relationships.
distractor_notes.C: Crawl is early-stage basics, before mapped service dependencies.
distractor_notes.D: CSDM explicitly models these relationships; they aren't excluded.

stem: A manufacturer is aligning CIs to CSDM and needs to model production-line monitoring systems as the technical services that deliver operational capability. Which CSDM domain do these technical services belong to?
rationale: Technical services that deliver IT/operational capability — including the application/technical services behind production-line monitoring — live in the Manage Technical Services domain. Sell/Consume covers business-facing offerings, Foundation holds core data, and Design holds business applications.

distractor_notes.B: Sell/Consume is about business service offerings consumed, not the technical services delivering them.
distractor_notes.C: Foundation holds core reference data, not technical services.
distractor_notes.D: Design holds business applications and architecture, not the running technical services.

stem: Why is Data Foundations / CSDM considered a prerequisite for ServiceNow implementation specialty tracks?

options.text: Because a correctly structured, CSDM-aligned CMDB underpins the service data that ITSM, ITOM, SecOps, and other applications rely on
Because it is only about visual themes
Because it is unrelated to other ServiceNow products

rationale: Nearly every ServiceNow application consumes CMDB/service data, so getting that foundation right — structured per CSDM — is the bedrock the specialty implementations build on. That's why Data Foundations is positioned as a prerequisite across the CIS tracks.

distractor_notes.B: CSDM is a data framework, not visual theming.
distractor_notes.C: It enables, rather than disables, other applications.
distractor_notes.D: It is foundational to many products, the opposite of unrelated.

stem: Several teams list desired use cases. Which one generally requires a HIGHER level of CSDM maturity to deliver well?

options.text: Business Service Management understanding the operational impact across mapped services
Storing a basic list of laptops with no relationships
Adding one user to the user table

rationale: Understanding operational impact across services depends on mapped services and rich relationships — capabilities that come at higher CSDM maturity (Walk/Run). The other use cases are basic Foundation-level data entry that requires little maturity to satisfy.

distractor_notes.B: A flat laptop list with no relationships is low-maturity Foundation data.
distractor_notes.C: A single location record is basic Foundation data.
distractor_notes.D: Adding a user is trivial reference-data entry, not high maturity.

stem: A team is starting their CSDM journey and asks where to begin. Which area should be established first?

options.text: The Foundation domain (core data like organizations, locations, users)
Full application service mapping for every app

rationale: CSDM maturity starts at 'crawl' with Foundation data — organizations, locations, users, and groups — because everything else depends on it. Service mapping and richer modeling come in later stages.

distractor_notes.B: Full service mapping is a later (run/fly) activity, not the starting point.
distractor_notes.C: Predictive Intelligence is unrelated to where CSDM begins.
distractor_notes.D: Retiring CIs isn't a CSDM starting step.

stem: You need to represent 'SAP' as the deployable piece of software the business recognizes, separate from any running instance. Which CSDM concept fits?
rationale: A Business Application represents the recognizable software capability (like SAP) at a design level, while an Application Service represents a specific running/deployed instance that delivers it. Keeping them distinct is core to CSDM.

distractor_notes.B: An Application Service is the running instance, not the design-level application.
distractor_notes.C: A Service Offering is a specific offering with commitments, not the application itself.
distractor_notes.D: A Technical Service Offering is an offering of a technical service.

stem: Operations needs to see a specific running deployment of an app mapped to the servers and databases it depends on, for impact analysis. Which CSDM CI represents that running, mapped service?
rationale: An Application Service represents a deployed, running instance and is what Service Mapping populates with relationships to its supporting infrastructure — exactly what impact analysis needs.

distractor_notes.B: A Business Application is the design-level software, not the mapped running instance.
distractor_notes.C: An Information Object classifies data, not a running service.
distractor_notes.D: A Product Model describes a model of a product, not a running service.

stem: A service is provided in Gold and Silver tiers with different SLAs and price. How should these tiers be modeled in CSDM?

options.text: As separate Service Offerings of the same service
As duplicate CIs with no relationship

rationale: Different commitment tiers (Gold/Silver) are modeled as distinct Service Offerings under the same service, each carrying its own SLAs and terms. That keeps the catalog and commitments clean.

distractor_notes.B: Tiers aren't separate applications; they're offerings of one service.
distractor_notes.C: Information Objects classify data, not service tiers.
distractor_notes.D: Unrelated duplicates lose the relationship to the parent service.

stem: A CMDB was populated ad hoc, and now Change, Event Management, and SecOps struggle to use the data consistently. What does adopting CSDM provide?

options.text: A prescriptive, standard framework for modeling data so downstream products work consistently

rationale: CSDM is a prescriptive standard for how to structure CMDB data so that service-aware products (Change, Event Management, SecOps, and more) can rely on consistent, well-formed records. It's a blueprint, not a tool you install.

distractor_notes.B: CSDM is a data model standard, not a performance feature.
distractor_notes.C: It doesn't encrypt data.
distractor_notes.D: It complements IRE; it doesn't replace identification/reconciliation.

stem: Service Offerings and Application Services keep referencing missing companies and locations. Which CSDM area should be completed to fix this dependency?
rationale: Foundation data (companies, locations, users, groups) underpins the rest of CSDM. If offerings and services reference missing foundation records, completing the Foundation domain resolves the gaps.

distractor_notes.B: Patterns relate to discovery/service mapping, not foundational reference data.
distractor_notes.C: Predictive Intelligence is unrelated to foundation data.
distractor_notes.D: Portal theming is cosmetic.

stem: A team wants their Application Service CIs to accurately reflect real infrastructure dependencies rather than being maintained by hand. Which approach achieves this?

options.text: Use Service Mapping/Discovery to populate the Application Service relationships
Store dependencies in a knowledge article

rationale: Service Mapping (and Discovery) automatically populate and maintain the relationships under an Application Service, keeping the map accurate as infrastructure changes — far better than manual upkeep.

distractor_notes.B: Manual maintenance is unsustainable and goes stale.
distractor_notes.C: A knowledge article isn't a live, queryable dependency map.
distractor_notes.D: Disabling IRE harms data integrity.

stem: An organization has solid Foundation data and some Application Services, and wants a sensible next step in CSDM maturity. What is a reasonable progression?

options.text: Advance through the crawl-walk-run-fly stages, expanding service modeling and mapping
Skip straight to retiring the CMDB

rationale: CSDM is adopted incrementally through crawl-walk-run-fly, progressively maturing service modeling and mapping. With Foundation in place, expanding service and mapping coverage is the natural next step.

distractor_notes.B: Retiring the CMDB defeats the purpose.
distractor_notes.C: Free-form modeling reintroduces the inconsistency CSDM solves.
distractor_notes.D: Deleting Foundation data breaks everything that depends on it.

stem: An IT team provides a 'Database Hosting' technical service internally with specific commitments to other IT teams. How is the committed, consumable form of this technical service modeled?
rationale: A Technical Service Offering represents the committed, consumable offering of a technical service (like database hosting) with its terms — the technical counterpart to a business Service Offering.

distractor_notes.B: A Business Application is design-level software, not a service offering.
distractor_notes.C: Information Objects classify data.
distractor_notes.D: Product Models describe product models, not service commitments.

stem: Leadership questions why following CSDM is worth the effort. Which is the strongest justification?

options.text: Consistent, service-aware data unlocks reliable reporting, impact analysis, and downstream products
It makes the homepage load faster
It removes the need for any governance

rationale: CSDM's payoff is trustworthy, service-aware data that powers accurate reporting, impact analysis, and the many products that consume the CMDB. It complements governance rather than removing it.

distractor_notes.B: CSDM is about data structure, not page performance.
distractor_notes.C: Governance is still essential; CSDM works with it.
distractor_notes.D: CSDM doesn't encrypt data.

stem: Which TWO statements about CSDM are correct?

options.text: It is a prescriptive standard/blueprint for structuring CMDB data
Foundation data underpins the other domains
It is a plugin that auto-populates all CIs for you
It replaces the need for Discovery

rationale: CSDM is a prescriptive framework, and Foundation data is the base the rest builds on. It isn't an auto-populating plugin and it doesn't replace Discovery — those still ingest the data CSDM organizes.

distractor_notes.C: CSDM is a model/standard, not an auto-populating product.
distractor_notes.D: Discovery and other ingestion still populate the CMDB; CSDM structures it.

stem: Which TWO correctly distinguish a Business Application from an Application Service?

options.text: A Business Application is the design-level software the business recognizes
An Application Service is a deployed, running instance mapped to its infrastructure
They are the same record with two names
An Application Service cannot have relationships to CIs

rationale: A Business Application is the recognizable design-level software; an Application Service is the running, mapped instance with relationships to supporting CIs. They are distinct, related records.

distractor_notes.C: They are separate, related concepts, not one record.
distractor_notes.D: Application Services are specifically the CIs that carry infrastructure relationships.
